title: I have made programmable trading platform for traders who want to code strategies | dashboards | ML models | indicators
author: AcanthocephalaNo6605
selftext:
Two founder, been building this for a while. Posting the full walkthrough because the last thing I want is to describe it badly in text.

The Python part. There is a code editor inside the platform. You write a class, register it, and it shows up in the chart's indicator list next to the built-in ones, recomputing on every closed bar. Same idea for panels: declare a layout in Python and it docks like any other panel. In the video that is a gradient-boosting model predicting the next day's range, and a Bank Nifty heatmap.

The agentic part. There is an assistant in the same window. You ask in plain words, it reads what you have open, writes the Python into your workspace, runs it, and lists every step it took. In the video it writes the indicator, the model panel, and a backtest of six strategies across the top ten NIFTY stocks over three years, with a cost per trade and no look-ahead. It writes and runs code. It does not place orders and it cannot start a strategy live. That is deliberate.

Execution. Your broker stays your broker. IBKR and Alpaca are connected, plus Upstox and Zerodha for India. A strategy subscribes to bars, decides, and its orders go down the same path as a click on Buy: the same checks, your own limits, then to your broker's account. Kill switch, cancel all, square off all. Nothing trades until you arm it from the panel yourself.

What it is not. Not HFT. No agent that re-tunes a running strategy. Backtests are real history, not promises. Paper and live are separated in the engine, not by a setting.

Join the wait list today at https://while25.com/waitlist

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
Backtest to deploy in one workspace is a sensible shape, and what decides whether it is trustworthy is how you fill orders in the test. Daily bars with an assumed spread behaves very differently from a real quote at the timestamp, and for anything multi leg on options that gap is not small.

Also worth being explicit about whether the assistant writing a strategy can see the test period while it iterates. That loop is very easy to build and very hard to notice once it has flattered a few results.

What does the fill model use for options, mid of the chain or something closer to the actual quote?

replies.author: AcanthocephalaNo6605
replies.body:
Fair points, both of them.  
To be straight about where we are: there is no built-in backtest engine yet. Strategies run on an open Python SDK. Right now the fill logic is whatever you write yourself. So the assumptions are yours, and nothing is hidden behind a default.

We are integrating NautilusTrader as the backtest layer. It can fill against quote and order book data, not just bars. That matters most for the multi-leg options case you raised.

Your point about the assistant seeing the test period is a good one. We'll keep it in mind as the backtester comes together.
